title: Psychology of Horror: What Your Favorite Movie Says About You
summary: Scream 7 and Obsession show how different horror taste can be. See what the psychology of horror says your favorite movie may reveal about you.
body_markdown:
## What Your Favorite Horror Movie Says About You


1.


#### **Scream, Halloween, Friday the 13th:** Familiarity over surprise.


The plots change, but the formula doesn’t. Knowing what’s coming may make it more enjoyable. In a study published in[Psychological Science](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/0956797611417007) , people reported liking stories more when they knew the ending. The researchers suggested it may be because the story is easier for the brain to process. That comfort of knowing can also open the door to nostalgia. Rewatching these franchise classics may bring you back to the first time you saw one: who you were with, what year it was, how it felt. That can be a[psychological benefit](https://doi.org/10.1037/gpr0000109) , offering comfort and a connection to your past.


2.


#### **Obsession, The Conjuring, The Exorcist:** Possibility over proof.


These movies lean on things science can't explain: demons, possession, a supernatural wish. That same 2020 survey found that people who believe in the paranormal are drawn to supernatural horror. Those who believe less tend to prefer more realistic threats, like a slasher or a home invasion. In other words, people seek out the threats they find believable. If a ghost story scares you more than a masked killer, that may say something about what you believe is possible.


3.


#### **Backrooms, Smile, The Blair Witch Project:** Curiosity over certainty.


These movies hold back the full picture. A basement leads to endless rooms. A[psychiatrist sees smiling faces](https://lifestance.com/podcasts/smile/) no one else can see. Three student filmmakers go looking for a local legend and get lost in the woods. A[2024 study in the Journal of Neuroscience](https://www.jneurosci.org/content/44/33/e0974232024) found that curiosity peaks when our confidence is low. The less certain a situation feels, the more our brain wants to understand it. That pull to find answers may be exactly what hooks you on this kind of horror.


4.


#### **Terrifier, Evil Dead, Saw:** Intensity over restraint.


Researchers behind the 2020 survey found that sensation seeking predicts how much a person enjoys horror and how often they watch it. People high in sensation seeking also tend to expect good feelings from horror, not just fear. If the gore in these movies feels fun instead of hard to sit through, you may simply enjoy a higher level of intensity.


5.


#### **Ghostbusters, Hocus Pocus, Beetlejuice:** Fun over fear.


Some favorites keep the scares light. They can still spook some viewers, but for many people they feel fun and safe at the same time. If your favorite “horror” movie is really a comedy in a costume, you may be drawn to the mood and ritual of Halloween more than to fear itself.


Fear from a horror movie is the kind you choose. That’s a big part of[why people enjoy being scared](https://lifestance.com/blog/why-people-like-to-be-scared-fears-explained/) . You can pause it, look away, or turn on the lights. But if worry follows you after the credits, or[anxiety](https://lifestance.com/condition/generalized-anxiety-disorder/) is getting harder to manage, a[mental health care provider](https://lifestance.com/provider/) can help provide support.
